title: Nutty Bengali Nuts Poha Balls
description: Salty, crumbly, sick-day indian dish featuring nuts, perfect for days when you're feeling under the weather. This dairy-free-friendly recipe is inspired by the flavors of Bengal, with a twist of poha (flattened rice flakes).
instructions: Mix poha, almonds, pistachios, cumin seeds, mustard seeds, chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Heat ghee or vegan oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat.
Add the poha mixture to the pan and stir constantly for about 10 minutes, or until the mixture is lightly toasted and fragrant.
Add lemon juice and honey (if using) to the mixture and stir well.
Shape the mixture into small balls, about 1-inch in diameter.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the poha balls in batches until they are golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per batch.
Remove the fried poha balls from the oil with a slotted spoon and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the Nutty Bengali Nuts Poha Balls hot, garnished with chopped nuts and a sprinkle of salt, if desired.
